reset: Reset puts the original settings.json back.
title: Schedule a pipeline and trigger it when a file lands
objective_text: Set a pipeline's nightly schedule and a storage event trigger that starts it for each new file, passing the right parameters to each.
scenario: Load orders runs a full reload every night and should also pick up partner files as they land during the day. The current schedule runs at the wrong hour, never ends, and sends a parameter the pipeline ignores. There's no file trigger yet.
engine_label: A model of a pipeline's schedule and storage event trigger, checked on this PC
verifies: Your schedule and trigger start the pipeline at the right times with the right parameters, as the pipeline runs page describes them, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That the schedule or trigger fires in Fabric: nothing is scheduled here.
The exact names Fabric shows for time zones, event types and filters; the model uses its own fields.
Interval-based schedules (preview) and OneLake event triggers.

expected.description: A daily 02:00 W. Europe Standard Time schedule from 2026-11-07 to 2027-12-31 with run_mode full, and a BlobCreated trigger on orders/*.csv with run_mode incremental and the trigger's file name.

validation.fail: The nightly schedule won't run as the team needs.
validation.pass: One schedule: daily at 02:00 Amsterdam time, with an end date and the right parameter.

rules.why: A schedule runs in the time zone it names; 02:00 UTC is 03:00 in Amsterdam in winter.
A schedule needs both a start and an end date; there's no open-ended schedule.
Parameter names in a schedule must match the pipeline's; a mismatched name is ignored at run time.

validation.fail: The file trigger would start on the wrong events or load the wrong file.
validation.pass: New .csv files in orders start an incremental run for that file.

rules.why: The files land in an Azure Blob Storage account, not OneLake.
Only created files start a run.
The subject filter narrows events by folder, file name and file type.
The trigger passes the file that started it; a fixed name would load the same file every time.

hints: Which time zone is Amsterdam in? Is UTC the same at 02:00 in November?
Compare the schedule's parameter names with the pipeline's, character by character.
Which event types mean a new file? Which would start a run when a file is deleted?
The trigger can pass the name of the file that started it: @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName.
explanation: A schedule needs a frequency, a time, a time zone, and both a start and an end date. Its parameters go to the pipeline by name, and a name that doesn't match is ignored, so RunMode never reached run_mode. A storage event trigger starts the pipeline on events from a storage account; choosing only BlobCreated and filtering the subject by folder and file type keeps deletes and other files out. Passing @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName lets each run load the file that started it.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-06 (pipeline-runs): schedules take a type, frequency, start and end, and time zone; start and end are both required; schedule parameter names must match the pipeline's and mismatches are ignored; storage event triggers choose OneLake or Azure Blob events, event types such as Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated, a Subject filter by folder, file name and file type, and pass @pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName.
W. Europe Standard Time is the Windows time zone id for Amsterdam; the model doesn't claim it's the label Fabric's picker shows.
